subject: Mutual Action Plan: embedded activation, canary & training surge

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Mutual Action Plan: embedded activation, canary & training surge

Hi Daniel —

Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that embeds the post-signature implementation milestones we discussed: rollout windows, a canary approach, migration cutover steps, and the training surge for your ops and CS teams. Key asks from our side are noted in the "Action" column.

High-level proposal (dates are placeholders until you confirm availability):
- Week 0 (Sep 20): Provisioning & network validation (VPC peering + KMS handshake)
- Week 1 (Sep 27): Canary 1 (5% traffic, smoke tests, 48-hour validation)
- Week 2 (Oct 4): Canary 2 (25% traffic, full acceptance tests)
- Week 3 (Oct 11): Cutover window (incremental shift + monitoring)
- Training surge: two-day live workshops (Sep 29 and Oct 6) + on-demand playbook

Acceptance gates we propose:
- Security/compliance: KMS logs and auditor checklist signed off
- Latency: 99th pctl within agreed SLA on sample queries
- Quality: evaluation set scores within 5% of pre-signature baseline

Attachments: Lumina_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP with owner assignments and dates). I also included a short checklist in the sheet named "Canary Test Spec" — we'll formalize that into a PDF after we lock scope.

Can you confirm: (1) whether the week-of dates above are workable for Lumina, (2) who will own the acceptance gate sign-offs on your side (security, platform, product), and (3) whether you prefer a single two-day training block or two one-day sessions?

If that works, we can convert the MAP to a shared Drive doc and add the HubSpot deal link for traceability.

Thanks —
Ben

Ben —

Thanks for the detailed MAP and the attachment. High level this looks reasonable. A few quick clarifications before we confirm dates: 

- Canary sizing: can you confirm rollback criteria? If Canary 1 shows a regression in the evaluation set, what's the guaranteed rollback window and owner?
- Training: our CS lead prefers two half-day sessions (to reduce scheduling conflict) rather than a single two-day block. Any problems with that?
- Acceptance owners: I will own Product sign-off, Sarah Torres (security@luminahealth.com) will own compliance, and Michael Lee (platform@luminahealth.com) will own the infra/network acceptance. I'll loop them in once dates are locked.

Also — do you have a separate doc for the canary test scripts and monitoring hooks? We want to review alert thresholds ahead of the canary start.

Daniel

Daniel —

Appreciate the quick feedback. Short answers and updates below; see inline acceptance-owner matrix and revised schedule in the attached Canary_Test_Specs.pdf.

Rollback/guardrails:
- Rollback window: we hold at the current stable model instance and revert traffic within 30 minutes if critical errors or a drop >7% on the evaluation pass-rate persist for two consecutive 15-minute intervals. Redwood ops (owner: Vanessa) will execute rollback; Lumina Product or Platform may call for an immediate stop.
- Monitoring hooks: will include token-level latency, end-to-end SLO checks, and automatic alerting to both teams' PagerDuty channels. Thresholds are in the attached PDF.

Canary sizing (revised):
- Canary 1: 5% traffic, 48-hour observation
- Canary 2: 25% traffic, 72-hour observation
- Progressive ramp to 100% across a 6-hour window during cutover with manual hold points

Training preference: two half-day sessions is fine. We'll run an instructor-led workshop (2 x 4-hour blocks) and provide recorded sessions plus a playbook. Proposed slots: Sep 29 (AM) and Oct 6 (AM).

Owners (finalizing):
- Security/compliance: Sarah Torres (Lumina) — will be added to the Drive doc for evidence upload
- Product acceptance: Daniel Park (Lumina)
- Infra/network: Michael Lee (Lumina)
- Redwood ops (rollback/execution): Vanessa Ortiz
- Redwood training & enablement: Marissa Cole

Next steps:
1) Ben to move the MAP to a shared Drive doc and add HubSpot deal link.
2) Lumina to confirm Sarah/Michael availability for acceptance gates.
3) Redwood to deliver Canary_Test_Specs.pdf (attached) and a short runbook for cutover day.

Attaching: Canary_Test_Specs.pdf (9 pages).

Thanks —
Marissa
